title: Data Center Is Fined $1.1 Million for Operating 62 Power Generators

reading.body:
This is a compliance failure at the build-out and operating stage of a facility, not a failure of a model or a decision system. The 62 natural-gas generators at the Vineland site were installed and run without the permits New Jersey requires, and the state treated that as a violation of its Air Pollution Control Act. The gap sits in the physical deployment of the campus, at the point where equipment is commissioned and energised, rather than in anything the reporting describes as software.

Catching it would have taken a permit review before the generators were installed or started, and an internal check that the equipment actually running on site matched what had been authorised. State inspectors found the generators in late July, so the condition was identified by a regulator rather than by the operator. The reporting does not say what internal compliance checks DataOne had in place.

What is not established is whether the generators were operated without permits knowingly, and the federal lawsuit from homeowners over noise is an allegation that the reporting does not describe as adjudicated. The reporting also does not establish what computing workloads the campus serves.

reports.title: Data Center Is Fined $1.1 Million for Operating 62 Power Generators

summary:
On Tuesday, New Jersey fined DataOne $1.07 million after state inspectors found 62 natural-gas generators at its Vineland data center site in late July. The 2,000-kilowatt generators lacked required permits to be installed or operated. The penalty was for violating the state's Air Pollution Control Act and is the largest ever issued to a data center operator in New Jersey, officials said. The campus is planned as a 2.6 million-square-foot complex needing 350 megawatts, enough to power a medium-size city, and is slated for completion at the end of the year.

Some of the complex is already in use. It has drawn complaints, including a federal lawsuit from homeowners over persistent noise and violation orders from the Cumberland County Health Department for excessive noise. Governor Mikie Sherrill said at a Climate Week event that data center development must benefit New Jersey communities.
